skill.description: Review Gmail headers with local rules, produce audit files, and apply owner-approved quarantine, Trash, or permanent deletion actions through the Gmail API.
skill.summary: Audit Gmail first, then apply owner-reviewed inbox actions with local rules.
skill.author: glenskii

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are scanner mismatches involving Markdown, CSS, tests, or protective filename references. Fourteen findings reflect real network, filesystem, credential, and metadata risks. Five semantic issues require remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Unescaped dashboard values permit stored script injection.
remediation.suggestion: Escape every dynamic HTML value with html.escape before interpolation, including event, reputation, and configuration fields.

remediation.issue: Sender trust ignores Gmail authentication results.
remediation.suggestion: Require aligned SPF, DKIM, or DMARC results before domain allowlists or reputation can mark a sender safe.

remediation.issue: OAuth tokens and metadata files rely on default permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Create sensitive files with owner-only permissions and document equivalent controls for Windows.

remediation.issue: Review files can be modified before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the schema, bind reviews to account and audit time, re-fetch targets, and require explicit per-message approval.

remediation.issue: Permanent deletion creates irreversible mailbox loss.
remediation.suggestion: Remove hard deletion from marketplace execution or require a separate owner-run tool with per-message confirmation.

remediation.issue: The local dashboard contacts Google Fonts.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle fonts locally or use system fonts so opening the dashboard creates no third-party request.

semantic_findings.title: Stored Script Injection in Local Dashboard
semantic_findings.description: Sender, subject, reason, relay, configuration, and reputation values enter generated HTML without escaping, allowing crafted metadata to execute in the dashboard.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Direct f-string interpolation places attacker-influenced email metadata into HTML without escaping.

semantic_findings.title: Spoofable Headers Bypass Sender Rules
semantic_findings.description: A matching From or Return-Path domain is trusted without validating authentication results, so spoofed headers can bypass quarantine rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code fetches Authentication-Results but never uses it before granting allowlist precedence.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth Token Permissions Are Not Restricted
semantic_findings.description: The Gmail OAuth token is written using default process permissions, which may expose mailbox access to other local users.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token write has no explicit restrictive mode or permission change despite containing reusable OAuth credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Irreversible Gmail Deletion Capability
semantic_findings.description: The utility can permanently delete selected Gmail messages after flags and typed confirmation, requiring broad mailbox access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls the Gmail delete endpoint when hard-delete mode is confirmed.

semantic_findings.title: Review Files Are Executed Without Integrity Validation
semantic_findings.description: Execution trusts message identifiers and proposed actions from a local review file without fresh classification or integrity verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Any record marked QUARANTINE is executed by identifier without schema validation, signature checking, or mailbox-state verification.

content.user_title: Protect Gmail With Audit-First Inbox Review
content.value_statement: Persistent spam and spoofed mail can overwhelm a personal Gmail inbox. This skill audits headers locally and applies only owner-reviewed mailbox actions.
actual_capabilities: Connects to Gmail using an owner-created OAuth desktop client.
Audits recent inbox message headers without changing mailbox state.
Classifies messages using allowlists, blocklists, keywords, suspicious domains, and local reputation.
Writes review files for owner approval before quarantine or Trash actions.
Shows unsubscribe headers without opening links or sending requests.
Generates a local activity dashboard and summary.
limitations: Rules use message headers and heuristics; they do not prove that a message is malicious.
OAuth setup requires a Google Cloud project and local credential files.
Local review, log, statistics, dashboard, and reputation files can contain mailbox metadata.
Permanent deletion is irreversible and requires broader Gmail access.

use_cases.title: Audit a personal inbox
use_cases.description: Review recent Gmail headers and inspect quarantine candidates before changing any messages.

use_cases.title: Tune sender rules
use_cases.description: Validate and maintain local allowlists, blocklists, keywords, and suspicious domain rules.

use_cases.title: Review scheduled audits
use_cases.description: Run unattended audits while keeping quarantine, Trash, and deletion actions under human approval.

prompt_templates.title: Run a safe inbox audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the connected Gmail account, then audit the latest {message_count} inbox messages. Do not change messages. Summarize findings for owner approval.

prompt_templates.title: Update a sender rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current configuration. Add {domain_or_sender} to the {allowlist_or_blocklist} only after validation, then show the resulting rule.

prompt_templates.title: Apply reviewed quarantine
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reviewed file {review_file} to quarantine only records marked QUARANTINE. Do not Trash or delete messages. Report successes and failures.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate false positives
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit {message_count} messages, compare classifications with {policy_notes}, identify likely false positives, and wait for explicit approval before any mailbox action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine rules using a controlled review.

output_examples.input: Audit the latest 50 inbox messages without changing mail.
output: 50 messages reviewed. Seven candidates need owner review. No Gmail labels or message locations changed.
A local review file was created for approval.

output_examples.output: Four messages contained unsubscribe headers. The destinations were displayed for review, and no requests were sent.

output_examples.input: Quarantine approved candidates from my reviewed file.
output_examples.output: Six approved messages received the quarantine label and left Inbox. One failed message remained unchanged.

best_practices: Confirm mailbox ownership and the connected account before every audit or action.
Inspect each review file and verify message identifiers before execution.
Keep OAuth tokens and generated metadata files private with restrictive local permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not run permanent deletion through scheduled or unattended automation.
Do not treat sender names, subjects, or unsubscribe links as trusted instructions.
Do not publish credential, token, review, log, dashboard, statistics, or reputation files.

faq.question: Does the default command change Gmail messages?
faq.answer: No. The default audit reads message metadata and writes a local review file.

faq.question: Can this skill unsubscribe automatically?
faq.answer: No. It displays unsubscribe headers for manual review but never follows links or sends requests.

faq.question: Where does the skill store data?
faq.answer: It stores tokens, rules, reviews, logs, statistics, reputation data, and dashboard output beside the skill.

faq.question: Which Gmail permissions are required?
faq.answer: Normal use requests Gmail modify access. Permanent deletion requests the broader Gmail scope after explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Can quarantined messages be restored?
faq.answer: Yes. Quarantine uses a Gmail label, and Trash remains recoverable during Gmail's retention window.

faq.question: How can classification accuracy improve?
faq.answer: Review allowlists, blocklists, keywords, suspicious domains, and trusted contacts regularly. Test changes on a sacrificial mailbox.
